findings.title: No test fails when the output <pre> loses tabIndex, role and aria-label
findings.scenario: Fix claim (5) says the output <pre> scrolls and is focusable. I deleted the line `tabIndex={0}` from the <pre> in apps/web/src/pages/session/parts.tsx (line 203) and ran the whole suite: 579 of 579 passed. A later edit can remove the attribute (the eslint-disable comment above it invites that), and a keyboard user can no longer scroll a long output. The gate stays green.
findings.evidence: Mutation (p): removed `tabIndex={0}`. Result: Test Files 51 passed, Tests 579 passed. `grep -n 'tabindex|tabIndex|role=|region' parts.test.tsx` finds nothing. renderToStaticMarkup does emit tabindex="0", role="region" and aria-label="run output", so one `toContain` line in the existing output test closes it.

findings.title: The childTaskIds half of the appendStep guard has no test
findings.scenario: I changed the guard in kernel.ts line 176 to `if (kind === 'delegate')`. All 579 tests passed. The test named 'does not let a worker name child tasks' always sends kind 'delegate' with the childTaskIds, so the first half of the `||` answers and the second half never decides. A worker that sends kind 'tool' with detail.childTaskIds is the case the second half exists for. The damage is small: checkedDetail() drops childTaskIds anyway, so the mutant stores nothing wrong; it only stops throwing.
findings.evidence: Mutation (d2): 579 passed. Mutation (d1), which keeps only the childTaskIds half, fails 'session: kernel, what a step carries > does not charge a step whose cost is zero, and does not let a worker name child tasks'. Add one assertion: appendStep(id, 'tool', 'x', { childTaskIds: ['t'] }) rejects.

findings.title: The Stop button's click is not tested, and Session.tsx has no test
findings.scenario: I removed `onClick={onStop}` from the Stop button in parts.tsx. All 579 tests passed: the suite renders to a string and passes noop handlers, so it proves the button is drawn and not that it stops anything. The same is true of every Session.tsx claim in fix (5): focus moves to the stream, findings are refetched when the socket reopens, the clock ticks at once, the stream scrolls inside the card. Only apps/web/src/main.tsx imports Session.tsx. vitest.config.ts says so openly ('A test that needs clicks gets a DOM environment when the first one lands'), so this is a known limit. The fix commit title says 'the page is tested'; the parts are tested, the page is not.
findings.evidence: Mutation (r): removed onClick={onStop}; 579 passed. `grep -rln "pages/session/Session" apps/web/src` returns main.tsx only.

findings.title: The pace-0 test asserts exact [0, 0] from two Date.now() reads
findings.scenario: work() reads Date.now() twice with no wait between at pace 0 and returns the difference. If the millisecond changes between the two reads, durationMs is 1 and `toEqual([0, 0])` fails. The window is about 100 ns in each 1 ms, two times per run, so about 1 failure in several thousand runs. It passed in each of my 25 full runs. `durations.every((ms) => ms <= 1)` or a check that the run finished in under the pace says the same thing without the race.
findings.evidence: demoWorker.ts lines 42-46: `const startedAt = Date.now(); if (paceMs > 0) await ...; return Date.now() - startedAt;`. Test line 53-55 expects exactly [0, 0]. The other timing test (paceMs 40, each duration >= 35, wall >= sum - 5) has enough slack; its second assertion is true by construction for any measured value and only catches an invented duration.
